In a new study, University of Delaware biogeochemist  Rachel Tabor  and her colleagues examine how these changes will affect Delaware’s coastal bays and sounds, and how they might be mitigated. Their research is published in the journal  Environmental Science & Technology.
The authors use the  National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s  (National Centers for Environmental Information’s) historical and future climate data to project how temperatures and ocean acidification will change in Delaware’s coastal waters by 2100.
They then run a series of computer simulations to estimate how changes in temperature and ocean acidification might affect the populations of different species of plants and animals in Delaware’s coastal bays and sounds.
